# Phase D — Building & Conveyor System

## What It Looks Like When Running

You open the shop, buy a "Conveyor Belt" item — a crate spawns near the elevator. Walk to it, press E → "Take" appears. The crate disappears and a ToolBuilder goes into your hotbar.

Equip the conveyor tool from hotbar. A transparent green ghost of the conveyor belt follows your camera aim, snapped to a 1m world grid. Move your mouse — the ghost slides along grid positions. Look at an invalid spot (overlapping another building) — ghost turns red. Press R — ghost rotates 90°. Press Q — ghost mirrors to an alternate variant. Place it near another conveyor — the system auto-snaps input→output by testing 4 rotations and picking the best alignment. Left-click — real conveyor belt instantiates at the ghost position. Tool quantity decreases. At 0, the tool is consumed.

Place multiple belts end-to-end. Drop an ore piece on the first belt. Watch it push forward along the chain, transitioning smoothly between belts. Shaker belts bounce ore left-right. Blocker gates stop the flow. Splitter arms alternate direction. Routing conveyors switch between two output paths on interaction.

Equip the hammer → look at any placed building → ObjectHighlighterManager outlines it. Press E → interaction wheel shows "Take" and "Pack". Take returns it to inventory. Pack spawns a crate on the ground.

Buildings on uneven ground get modular scaffolding legs that raycast downward and spawn dynamically. Toggle supports on/off with the wrench tool.

---

## Folder Structure

```
phase-d/Scripts/
├── 0-Core/
│   └── GameEvents.cs                           (partial: OnBuildingPlaced, OnBuildingRemoved, OnBuildingTakeRequested)
│
├── _-Systems/
│   ├── BuildingSystem/                          ← GAME-SPECIFIC (imports IInventoryItem, IInteractable, IHighlightable)
│   │   ├── BuildingObject.cs                    → "I'm a placed building with Take/Pack interactions"
│   │   ├── BuildingCrate.cs                     → "I'm a packed building crate on the ground"
│   │   ├── BuildingManager.cs                   → "I manage ghost preview + grid placement"
│   │   ├── BuildingDataService.cs               → "I validate grid + conveyor snap (pure C#)"
│   │   ├── BuildingPlacementNode.cs             → "I mark where specific buildings can attach"
│   │   ├── SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition.cs    → "I define a building's inventory identity"
│   │   ├── BaseModularSupports.cs               → "I'm the base class for scaffolding legs"
```

```csharp
// Key additions:
```

### 2. `phase-b/Scripts/_-Systems/ToolSystem/ToolBase.cs` (BaseHeldTool) — **ADD** protected write fields

ToolBuilder.Setup() needs to write `_name`, `_description`, `_maxAmount` which are private `[SerializeField]` fields on BaseHeldTool. Add protected write-only properties:

```csharp
// ← ADD inside BaseHeldTool class, after the #region private API section
#region protected write access — ToolBuilder.Setup() needs these
protected string toolName { set => _name = value; }
protected string toolDescription { set => _description = value; }
protected int toolMaxAmount { set => _maxAmount = value; }
#endregion
```

Without this, ToolBuilder.Setup() cannot configure the tool from its SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition.

### 3. `phase-b/Scripts/2-Data/Enums/GlobalEnumsB.cs` — **ADD** values

```csharp
public enum InteractionType
{
    take,
    destroy,
    toggle,    // ← ADD (ChuteHatch, ConveyorBlockerT2)
    pack,      // ← ADD (BuildingObject "Pack")
    switchDirection // ← ADD (RoutingConveyor)
}
```

### 4. `phase-b/Scripts/3-MonoBehaviours/Physics/BasePhysicsObject.cs` — **ADD** belt tracking methods

Phase B already has: `AddConveyorVelocity`, `ResetAccum`, `Rb`, `Count`, `SumVelocity`, `RetainY`, `BestY`.
Phase D's ConveyorBelt calls `AddTouchingConveyorBelt` / `RemoveTouchingConveyorBelt` which don't exist yet.
Also uncomment the `OnEnable`/`OnDisable` stubs to register with ConveyorBeltManager.

```csharp
// ← ADD after the existing #region public API section:
List<ConveyorBelt> touchingBelts = new List<ConveyorBelt>();

/// <summary> ConveyorBelt calls this on trigger enter to register itself. </summary>
public void AddTouchingConveyorBelt(ConveyorBelt belt)
{
    if (!touchingBelts.Contains(belt)) touchingBelts.Add(belt);
    ConveyorBeltManager.Register(this);
}

/// <summary> ConveyorBelt calls this on trigger exit to unregister itself. </summary>
public void RemoveTouchingConveyorBelt(ConveyorBelt belt)
{
    touchingBelts.Remove(belt);
    if (touchingBelts.Count == 0) ConveyorBeltManager.Unregister(this);
}

// ← MODIFY OnEnable/OnDisable — uncomment the stubs:
protected virtual void OnEnable()
{
    // → re-register if we still have belts touching us (re-enable after pool recycle)
    if (touchingBelts.Count > 0) ConveyorBeltManager.Register(this);
}
protected virtual void OnDisable()
{
    ConveyorBeltManager.Unregister(this);
}
```

### 5. `phase-a/Scripts/_-Systems/ShopUISystem/SO_ShopItemDef.cs` — **ADD** BuildingDefinition field + delegation

The original `ShopItemDefinition` has a `BuildingInventoryDefinition` field. When set, `GetName()`, `GetDescription()`, `GetIcon()`, `GetSavableObjectID()` all delegate to the building definition instead of using the shop item's own fields. This links shop items to building data.

```csharp
// ← ADD field:
[SerializeField] SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition _buildingDefinition;
[SerializeField] bool _useNameAndDescriptionOfBuildingDefinition;

// ← MODIFY GetName() to check building def first:
public string GetName()
{
    if (_useNameAndDescriptionOfBuildingDefinition && _buildingDefinition != null)
        return _buildingDefinition.Name;
    return _itemDefName;
}

// ← MODIFY GetDescription() same pattern
// ← MODIFY GetIcon() — if _buildingDefinition != null, return _buildingDefinition.GetIcon()
// ← ADD GetBuildingDefinition() => _buildingDefinition;
```

### 6. `phase-a/Scripts/_-Systems/EconomySystem/EconomyManager.cs` — **ADD** GetPriceOfBuildingDefinition

`BuildingCrate.GetSellValue()` calls this to look up the shop price of a building. Original EconomyManager stores `_allShopItemDefinitions` and searches for the matching `BuildingInventoryDefinition`.

```csharp
// ← ADD method:
/// <summary> Finds the ShopItemDef that links to this building definition and returns its price.
/// Returns 10f fallback if not found. BuildingCrate.GetSellValue() uses this × 0.9 × quantity. </summary>
public float GetPriceOfBuildingDefinition(SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition def)
{
    // → search all shop items for one that links to this building definition
    var shopItem = _allShopItemDefinitions.find(s => s.GetBuildingDefinition() == def);
    if (shopItem != null) return shopItem.GetDefaultPrice();
    Debug.Log($"Couldn't find ShopItem for BuildingDefinition: {def.Name}");
    return 10f;
}
```

### 7. `phase-c/Scripts/_-Systems/AutoMinerSystem/AutoMiner.cs` — already has SetResourceDefinition ✅

Phase C already includes `SetResourceDefinition(SO_AutoMinerResourceDefinition def)` — documented in comments as "Phase D: BuildingPlacementNode calls this". No additional modification needed.

## Source vs Phase Diff

| What | Original Source | Our Architecture |
|------|---------------|-----------------|
| Ghost management | `BuildingManager` has inline grid + snap math | Grid + snap split to `BuildingDataService` (pure C# testable) |
| BuildingObject interactions | Direct string comparison (`"Take"`, `"Pack"`) | Uses `InteractionType` enum via `SO_InteractionOption` |
| BuildingCrate.TryAddToInventory | `FindObjectOfType<PlayerInventory>()` | Fires `GameEvents.RaiseToolPickupRequested` |
| BuildingObject.TryAddToInventory | `FindObjectOfType<PlayerInventory>()` | Fires `GameEvents.RaiseBuildingTakeRequested` |
| ToolBuilder.DropItem | `FindObjectOfType<PlayerController>()` | Uses `ownerCam` from `SetOwnerContext` |
| Conveyor velocity | Inline in each belt's FixedUpdate | `ConveyorBeltManager` batch-applies from `BasePhysicsObject` accumulators |
| BuildingInventoryDefinition.GetIcon | Logic method on SO_ | Moved to `SO_BuildingInventoryDefinitionExt` extension class |
| Layer setting | `SetLayerRecursively` inside BuildingManager | Extracted to `UtilsPhaseD.SetLayerRecursively` |

### Individual Systems

| System | Scripts | Decoupling |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **BuildingSystem** | 13 scripts | `GameEvents.OnBuildingPlaced`, `OnBuildingRemoved`, `OnBuildingTakeRequested`. Uses `IInteractable`, `IHighlightable`, `IInventoryItem` interfaces. |

|------|--------|-------------|

**Final count:** 2 systems, 31 scripts (24 code + 2 utils + 2 enums/entities + 3 Phase G stubs), 2 `.cs` tests, 2 manual tests, 3 manual guides. Zero tight coupling between BuildingSystem and ConveyorSystem.

using System;

/// <summary>
/// Phase D partial — building placement, removal, and take events.
/// BuildingManager and ToolBuilder fire these. InventoryOrchestrator, QuestManager (Phase F),
/// and SaveSystem (Phase G) subscribe.
/// </summary>
public static partial class GameEvents
{
    // when building placed >>
    public static event Action<UnityEngine.Vector3> OnBuildingPlaced;
    public static void RaiseBuildingPlaced(UnityEngine.Vector3 position)
    {
        LogSubscribersCount(nameof(OnBuildingPlaced), OnBuildingPlaced);
        OnBuildingPlaced?.Invoke(position);
    }
    // << when building placed

    // when building removed (packed or taken) >>
    public static event Action<UnityEngine.Vector3> OnBuildingRemoved;
    public static void RaiseBuildingRemoved(UnityEngine.Vector3 position)
    {
        LogSubscribersCount(nameof(OnBuildingRemoved), OnBuildingRemoved);
        OnBuildingRemoved?.Invoke(position);
    }
    // << when building removed

    // when building take requested (hammer "Take" on BuildingObject) >>
    public static event Action<IInventoryItem> OnBuildingTakeRequested;
    public static void RaiseBuildingTakeRequested(IInventoryItem item)
    {
        LogSubscribersCount(nameof(OnBuildingTakeRequested), OnBuildingTakeRequested);
        OnBuildingTakeRequested?.Invoke(item);
    }
    // << when building take requested
}

using System;
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary> Save data for one placed BuildingObject — Phase G serializes these to JSON.
/// SavingLoadingManager reads the list on load, instantiates the prefab at Position/Rotation,
/// calls LoadBuildingSaveData to restore supports state + custom data. </summary>
[Serializable]
public class BuildingObjectEntry
{
    public SavableObjectID SavableObjectID;
    public float PosX, PosY, PosZ;
    public float RotX, RotY, RotZ;
    public bool BuildingSupportsEnable = true;
    public string CustomSaveData;

    public Vector3 GetPosition() => new Vector3(PosX, PosY, PosZ);
    public Vector3 GetRotation() => new Vector3(RotX, RotY, RotZ);
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-d(New)/Scripts/2-Data/Entities/BuildingRotationInfo.cs ==== -->
using System;
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary> One candidate snap rotation found by BuildingDataService.GetNearbySnapConnections.
/// BuildingManager groups these by Rotation, picks the most-voted one, and applies it
/// to the ghost so conveyor I/O aligns automatically. IsMirroredMode tracks whether
/// the Q-button mirror variant was used when this snap was calculated. </summary>
[Serializable]
public struct BuildingRotationInfo : IEquatable<BuildingRotationInfo>
{
    public Quaternion Rotation;
    public bool IsMirroredMode;

    public bool Equals(BuildingRotationInfo other) =>
        Rotation.Equals(other.Rotation) && IsMirroredMode == other.IsMirroredMode;

    public override bool Equals(object obj) => obj is BuildingRotationInfo other && Equals(other);
    public override int GetHashCode() => HashCode.Combine(Rotation, IsMirroredMode);
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-d(New)/Scripts/4-Utils/PhaseDLOG.cs ==== -->
using System.Linq;

/// <summary>
/// Phase D snapshot formatters — used by BuildingDataService.GetSnapshot() for test logging.
/// Formats conveyor belt counts and building placement node states.
/// </summary>
public static class PhaseDLOG
{
    /// <summary> Returns a snapshot string of all active conveyor belts (count + speeds). </summary>
    public static string CONVEYORBELT_SNAPSHOT()
    {
        var belts = ConveyorBelt.GetAllConveyorBelts();
        return $"[ConveyorBelts] count={belts.Count}, speeds=[{string.Join(", ", belts.Select(b => b.GetSpeed().ToString("F1")))}]";
    }

    /// <summary> Returns a snapshot string of all placement nodes (type + attached status). </summary>
    public static string PLACEMENT_NODE_SNAPSHOT()
    {
        var nodes = BuildingPlacementNode.GetAll();
        return $"[PlacementNodes] count={nodes.Count}, attached={nodes.Count(n => n.GetAttachedBuildingObject() != null)}";
    }
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-d(New)/Scripts/4-Utils/UtilsPhaseD.cs ==== -->
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary>
/// Phase D static helpers — SetLayerRecursively for ghost setup, IsFlatGround for placement checks.
/// </summary>
public static class UtilsPhaseD
{
    /// <summary> Sets the layer on a GO and all its children recursively. Used by BuildingManager
    /// to set ghost objects to the BuildingGhost layer, and by BuildingObject to set physical
    /// colliders to the BuildingObject layer. </summary>
    public static void SetLayerRecursively(GameObject obj, int newLayer)
    {
        if (obj == null) return;
        obj.layer = newLayer;
        foreach (Transform child in obj.transform)
        {
            if (child != null) SetLayerRecursively(child.gameObject, newLayer);
        }
    }
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-d(New)/Scripts/5-Tests/BuildingTest.cs ==== -->
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary>
/// Vertical slice test for BuildingSystem — place/rotate/snap/take/pack buildings without player.
///
/// Prerequisites: BuildingManager (singleton in scene), at least one SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition
/// with a BuildingObject prefab assigned, ToolBuilder prefab assigned to BuildingManager.
///
/// NOT required: PlayerMovement, PlayerCamera, ShopSystem, OreSystem, InventorySystem.
///
/// How to test:
/// 1. Press B → creates a ToolBuilder from the test definition, simulates equip
/// 2. Press R → rotates ghost 90°
/// 3. Press Q → cycles alternate prefab variants (mirror)
/// 4. Press Mouse0 → places building at ghost position if valid (green ghost)
/// 5. Press P → packs last placed building into a crate
/// 6. Press T → takes last placed building back into test slot
/// 7. Console shows: "[BuildingTest] placed at (x,y,z)", "[BuildingTest] removed at (x,y,z)"
///
/// Controls: B=create builder, R=rotate, Q=mirror, Mouse0=place, P=pack, T=take
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Tests/BuildingTest")]
public class BuildingTest : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition _testDefinition;
    [SerializeField] Camera _testCamera;

    ToolBuilder activeBuilder;

    private void Start()
    {
        Cursor.lockState = CursorLockMode.Locked;
        // purpose: log when a building is placed
        GameEvents.OnBuildingPlaced += pos => Debug.Log($"[BuildingTest] placed at {pos}");
        // purpose: log when a building is removed
        GameEvents.OnBuildingRemoved += pos => Debug.Log($"[BuildingTest] removed at {pos}");
        // purpose: log when a building take is requested
        GameEvents.OnBuildingTakeRequested += item => Debug.Log($"[BuildingTest] take requested: {item.GetName()}");
    }

    private void Update()
    {
        if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.B) && activeBuilder == null)
        {
            // → create ToolBuilder from test definition
            activeBuilder = Object.Instantiate(Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetBuildingToolPrefab());
            activeBuilder.SetDefinition(_testDefinition);
            activeBuilder.Setup();
            activeBuilder.gameObject.SetActive(true);
            Debug.Log("[BuildingTest] created builder tool");
        }
        if (activeBuilder != null)
        {
            // → simulate ghost update
            Vector3 aimPos = _testCamera.transform.position + _testCamera.transform.forward * 3f;
            Vector3Int gridPos = Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetClosestGridPosition(aimPos);
            activeBuilder.SimulateGhostUpdate(_testCamera, gridPos);

            if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.R)) activeBuilder.Reload();
            if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Q)) activeBuilder.QButtonPressed();
            if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Mouse0)) activeBuilder.PrimaryFire();
        }
    }
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-d(New)/Scripts/5-Tests/ConveyorTest.cs ==== -->
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary>
/// Vertical slice test for ConveyorSystem — ore flows along belt chain, all variants work.
///
/// Prerequisites: ConveyorBeltManager (singleton in scene), at least 3 ConveyorBelt prefabs
/// placed in a line, a Rigidbody sphere to simulate ore.
///
/// NOT required: PlayerMovement, ShopSystem, BuildingSystem, ToolSystem.
///
/// How to test:
/// 1. Press N → spawns a test sphere above the first belt
/// 2. Watch → sphere should move forward along belt chain
/// 3. Press M → toggles ConveyorBlocker (if present) — belt disables, ore stops
/// 4. Console shows: "[ConveyorTest] belt count: X", "[ConveyorTest] spawned ore"
///
/// Controls: N=spawn ore, M=toggle blocker
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Tests/ConveyorTest")]
public class ConveyorTest : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] GameObject _testOrePrefab;
    [SerializeField] Transform _spawnPoint;
    [SerializeField] ConveyorBlocker _testBlocker;

    private void Start()
    {
        Debug.Log($"[ConveyorTest] belt count: {ConveyorBelt.GetAllConveyorBelts().Count}");
        Debug.Log($"[ConveyorTest] batch render count: {ConveyorBatchRenderingComponent.GetAllConveyors().Count}");
    }

    private void Update()
    {
        if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.N) && _testOrePrefab != null && _spawnPoint != null)
        {
            Object.Instantiate(_testOrePrefab, _spawnPoint.position, Quaternion.identity);
            Debug.Log("[ConveyorTest] spawned ore");
        }
        if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.M) && _testBlocker != null)
        {
            Debug.Log("[ConveyorTest] toggling blocker");
        }
    }
}

# BuildingPlacementTest.md — Manual Test

## What This Tests

Ghost preview (green/red/orange), grid snap, rotation, mirror, conveyor auto-snap, take/pack interactions, and scaffolding supports. This is the full end-to-end building placement flow.

---

## Prerequisites

### Singletons Required
- **BuildingManager** — manages ghost lifecycle, materials, layers
- **UIManager** — for menu state reporting (Phase A)
- **EconomyManager** — for BuildingCrate sell value (Phase A)

### Layers Required (Edit → Project Settings → Tags and Layers)

| Layer Name | Layer # | What Fails If Missing |
|------------|---------|----------------------|
| BuildingObject | 8 (or next free) | Physical colliders not set, OverlapBox returns wrong results |
| BuildingGhost | 9 (or next free) | Ghost rendered as solid object, collides with world |

### Tags Required
- `Grabbable` — default tag on crates/ore (TagType.grabbable in GlobalEnumsAll.cs)

### SO Assets Required

## How It Works (System Flow)

**Ghost creation:** When `BuildingTest` presses B, it creates a `ToolBuilder` and calls `Setup()` — this copies the definition's Name, Description, and MaxStackSize. Each frame, `ToolBuilder.Update()` (or the test's simulation) calls `BuildingManager.UpdateGhostObject(gridPos, prefab, rotation, this)`. The first call to `SetupGhostObject` runs `Object.Instantiate(prefab)` → sets `IsGhost = true` → destroys all trigger collider GOs → disables all `MonoBehaviour`s except `BuildingObject` → disables `AudioSource`s → calls `UtilsPhaseD.SetLayerRecursively(ghostGO, BuildingGhostLayer)` → makes all `Rigidbody`s kinematic → disables `ParticleSystem`s. The ghost is now a visual-only shell.

**Ghost positioning:** After setup, ghost is moved to `gridPos + (0.5, 0, 0.5) + buildModePlacementOffset`. If the position changed from last frame, `isEligibleForSnapping` is set to true. Then `CanPlaceObject` is called to determine material color.

**Overlap check:** `CanPlaceObject` collects all `BoxCollider`s from the ghost's `BuildingPlacementColliderObject` children (falls back to `PhysicalColliderObject`). For each box, it calls `Physics.OverlapBox(center, halfExtents, rotation, layerMask)` — if anything overlaps, returns `CanPlaceBuilding.invalid` → **ghost turns red**.

**Flat ground check:** If the prefab has `RequiresFlatGround`, raycasts down from `(gridPos + 0.5, 0.1, 0.5)`. If no hit within 1m, or surface normal dot with `Vector3.up` < 0.9, or distance > 0.2 → returns `requirementsNotMet` → **ghost turns orange**.

**Conveyor snap:** If ghost has `ConveyorInputSnapPositions` and position just changed, `Physics.OverlapSphere(1.25m, BuildingObjectLayer)` finds neighbor buildings. For each neighbor, `BuildingDataService.GetNearbySnapConnections` tests 4 rotations × all input↔output pairs. Any pair within 0.25m adds a `BuildingRotationInfo` candidate. `ResolveBestSnap` groups by rotation, picks the most-voted, and applies it to the tool's `CurrentRotation`.

**Material swap:** Based on the result, all ghost renderers get materials replaced — green, red, or orange. Materials in `_materialsToNotReplaceOnBuildingGhost` are preserved (for transparent windows, etc.).

**Placement:** Left-click calls `PrimaryFire()` → `CanPlaceObject` one more time → if valid, `Object.Instantiate(selectedPrefab, ghostTransform.position, ghostTransform.rotation)`. If a `BuildingPlacementNode` was matched, `node.AttachBuilding(building)` stores the ref and configures AutoMiner. Quantity decrements.

---

   **EXPECT:** Console: `[BuildingTest] created builder tool`. A **transparent green ghost** appears where the camera aims, snapped to a 1m grid.

## Pitfall Checks

⚠️ **#5 Missing Layers:** If `BuildingObject` or `BuildingGhost` layers don't exist, `LayerMask.NameToLayer` returns -1. Ghost renders on Default layer (collides with everything). OverlapBox returns wrong results. **Verify:** Open any LayerMask field in inspector, both layers appear in dropdown.

⚠️ **#6 LayerMask at Nothing:** If `_buildingPlacementCollisionLayers` is left at "Nothing" (0), OverlapBox always returns empty → placement always valid → buildings overlap. **Verify:** Check every LayerMask field has correct layers checked.

⚠️ **#9 Static lists:** `ConveyorBelt.AllConveyorBelts` and `BuildingPlacementNode.All` survive domain reload. Second Play press may have stale null refs. Expected — round-robin cleanup handles it.

⚠️ **#10 Execution order:** `ConveyorBeltManager` has `[DefaultExecutionOrder(-10)]`. Do not remove it — velocity accumulation depends on running before belt FixedUpdate.

# ConveyorFlowTest.md — Manual Test

## What This Tests

Ore pieces flow along conveyor belt chains. All conveyor variants work correctly: shaker, blocker, splitter, routing. Batch rendering replaces individual renderers.

---

## Prerequisites

### Singletons Required
- **ConveyorBeltManager** — batch velocity application

### Layers Required
None specific to conveyors — belts use trigger colliders on Default layer.

---

## Setup Guide

### Step 1: Create ConveyorBeltManager GO
1. Create empty GO → name: `ConveyorBeltManager`
2. Add Component: `ConveyorBeltManager`

### Step 2: Create 3 ConveyorBelt GOs in a line
For each belt:
1. Create empty GO → name: `Belt_1`, `Belt_2`, `Belt_3`
2. Position them in a line: (0,0,0), (0,0,1), (0,0,2)
3. Each belt needs:
   - Add Component: `ConveyorBelt`
   - Create child GO named `TriggerZone`:
     - Add `BoxCollider`, set `IsTrigger = true`, size = (1, 0.2, 1)
   - Create child GO named `PhysicalSurface`:
     - Add `BoxCollider`, set `IsTrigger = false`, size = (1, 0.1, 1)
     - Add `MeshRenderer` + `MeshFilter` (cube mesh)

⚠️ **#8 Dual Collider Setup:** The trigger child detects entry/exit (`OnTriggerEnter`). The physical child prevents ore from falling through. If the trigger is missing or not flagged, ore sits on belt but doesn't move — no error in console.

### Step 3: Create test ore prefab
1. Create Sphere GO → name: `TestOre`
2. Add `Rigidbody` (mass = 0.1, useGravity = true)
3. Scale: (0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
4. Drag to Project to create prefab, delete scene instance

### Step 4: Create ConveyorTest GO
1. Create empty GO → name: `ConveyorTest`
2. Add Component: `ConveyorTest`
3. Wire:

| Field | Drag From |
|-------|----------|
| `_testOrePrefab` | Drag: TestOre prefab from Project |
| `_spawnPoint` | Create empty GO above Belt_1, drag from Hierarchy |

---

## How It Works (System Flow)

**Registration:** When a `ConveyorBelt` enables, it calculates `pushVelocity = transform.forward * Speed` and adds itself to the static `AllConveyorBelts` list. `ConveyorBeltManager` now knows it exists.

**Ore enters belt:** When the test ore (Rigidbody sphere) falls onto Belt_1's trigger child, `ConveyorBelt.OnTriggerEnter` fires. It gets the `attachedRigidbody`, finds or adds a `BasePhysicsObject` component, calls `AddPhysicsObject(bpo)` which adds to the belt's local list AND calls `bpo.AddTouchingConveyorBelt(this)` so the physics object knows which belts are pushing it.

**Velocity accumulation:** Each `FixedUpdate`, `ConveyorBelt` iterates its `physicsObjectsOnBelt` list and calls `bpo.AddConveyorVelocity(pushVelocity, retainYVelocity)`. Inside `BasePhysicsObject`, this **accumulates** into `conveyorSumVelocity` and increments `conveyorCount`. If the ore is on overlapping belts, it gets multiple contributions.

**Batch apply:** `ConveyorBeltManager.FixedUpdate()` runs **first** (due to `[DefaultExecutionOrder(-10)]`). For each registered `BasePhysicsObject` with `count > 0`: divides `sumVelocity / count` to get averaged velocity, handles Y-preservation, sets `rb.linearVelocity = result`, then resets accumulators. The ore now physically **moves forward** along the belt direction.

**Belt transition:** When the ore exits Belt_1's trigger, `OnTriggerExit` removes it from Belt_1's list. Simultaneously, Belt_2's `OnTriggerEnter` fires and adds it. The transition is seamless because both events happen in the same physics step.

**Shaker:** `ConveyorBeltShaker.FixedUpdate` replaces the base FixedUpdate. It calculates a sideways sine-wave component (`Mathf.Sign(Sin(time * 2π * freq))` gives square-wave direction) and a vertical sine, then adds both to the forward push velocity. The ore **bounces left-right and up-down** while moving forward.

**Blocker:** `ConveyorBlocker.Update()` reads `HingeJoint.angle`. If below -80°, sets `ConveyorBelt.SetDisabled(true)`. The belt's FixedUpdate early-returns when disabled. Ore stops being pushed.

**Round-robin cleanup:** `ConveyorBeltManager.Update()` picks one belt per frame and calls `ClearNullObjectsOnBelt()` — removes destroyed, inactive, or kinematic objects from the belt's list. This avoids iteration errors from destroyed ore.

---

## Manual Test Flow

1. **DO:** Press Play. Check console.
   **EXPECT:** `[ConveyorTest] belt count: 3`, `[ConveyorTest] batch render count: 0` (or 3 if batch rendering components present).

2. **DO:** Press N.
   **EXPECT:** Test sphere spawns above Belt_1, falls onto trigger, **starts moving forward** along Belt_1 → Belt_2 → Belt_3. Console: `[ConveyorTest] spawned ore`.
   *Behind the scenes:* `OnTriggerEnter` → `AddPhysicsObject` → belt accumulates velocity → `ConveyorBeltManager.FixedUpdate` applies → ore moves.

3. **DO:** Spawn 5 more spheres (press N rapidly).
   **EXPECT:** All spheres flow forward along belt chain. Some may push each other (physics interactions).

4. **DO:** (If ConveyorBeltShaker present) Observe ore on shaker belt.
   **EXPECT:** Ore **bounces left-right** while moving forward. Vertical bounce visible on full shaker.

5. **DO:** (If ConveyorBlocker present) Swing the hinge gate closed manually (or via test key M).
   **EXPECT:** Ore on that belt **stops moving**. Ore behind it piles up.

---

## Pitfall Checks

⚠️ **#8 Dual Collider Setup:** Each belt needs TWO colliders on separate child GOs. Trigger child (IsTrigger=true) detects entry/exit. Physical child (IsTrigger=false) is the surface. If trigger missing → `OnTriggerEnter` never fires → ore sits still, no error.

⚠️ **#9 Static lists:** `ConveyorBelt.AllConveyorBelts` is static. Second Play press may have stale refs. `ConveyorBeltManager.Update` round-robin cleans nulls — this is expected behavior.

⚠️ **#10 Execution order:** `ConveyorBeltManager` has `[DefaultExecutionOrder(-10)]`. Removing it causes velocity to be applied one frame late → physics stutters.

---

## Summary Checklist

- [ ] Ore flows forward along single belt
- [ ] Ore transitions smoothly between connected belts
- [ ] Shaker belt bounces ore left-right
- [ ] Blocker gate stops belt when closed
- [ ] Multiple ore pieces flow without errors
- [ ] Round-robin cleanup handles destroyed ore
- [ ] No console errors during 30 seconds of flow

# ScaffoldingTest.md — Manual Test

## What This Tests

Modular scaffolding legs raycast downward, spawn dynamically to reach the floor, use connector variants when landing on other support types, and toggle on/off with the wrench tool.

---

## Prerequisites

### Singletons Required
- **BuildingManager** — provides `BuildingSupportsCollisionLayers` and `ScaffoldingSupportsCollisionLayers`

### Layers Required

| Layer Name | What Fails If Missing |
|------------|----------------------|
| Default | Supports raycast against it — if excluded, legs never spawn |
| Terrain | Scaffolding supports raycast against it for terrain placement |

---

## Setup Guide

1. Place a BuildingObject prefab that has `ModularBuildingSupports` child components
2. Position it 3-5 units above the ground
3. Ensure ground has a collider on Default or Terrain layer

---

## How It Works (System Flow)

**Initial spawn:** When the BuildingObject instantiates in the scene, `BaseModularSupports.Start()` runs on each scaffolding child. It calls `GetComponentInParent<BuildingObject>()` to get the parent, then calls `SpawnSupports()`.

**ModularBuildingSupports.SpawnSupports:** Checks if supports are enabled on parent BuildingObject. Then `Physics.Raycast(position + rotatedOffset, Vector3.down, maxDistance, BuildingSupportsCollisionLayers)`. Calculates segment count: `Mathf.RoundToInt((hitDistance - raycastOffset.y) / supportSpacing) + 1`, clamped to `MaxSupports`.

**Connector check:** If the raycast hits another `ModularBuildingSupports` (stacked building), reads its `SupportType`. Based on the type (Roller, Conveyor, Chute, Walled), selects the appropriate connector prefab (e.g. `BottomToRollerPrefab`, `MiddleToConveyorPrefab`). If landing on `SupportType.none`, returns early (no legs). If landing on `SupportType.flat`, uses normal bottom cap.

**Instantiation:** Spawns top piece (if prefab assigned), N middle pieces at `SupportSpacing` intervals, and bottom cap with slight random rotation + scale for visual variety. All spawned GOs are parented to the support transform.

**ScaffoldingSupportLeg:** Simpler version — destroys existing children, raycasts down, spawns N copies of `SupportPrefab` at equal spacing. No connector variants.

**Respawn:** `BuildingObject.EnableBuildingSupports(bool)` (called by wrench tool) iterates all `BaseModularSupports` children and calls `RespawnSupports()`. This destroys all existing legs, clears the list, and re-runs `SpawnSupports()`.

**Update above:** When a building is placed or destroyed, `BuildingObject.UpdateSupportsAbove(isDestroyingThis)` temporarily disables its own colliders, raycasts up to find any `ModularBuildingSupports` above, and tells them to respawn. This ensures stacked buildings adjust their legs when the one below changes.

---

## Manual Test Flow

1. **DO:** Place a building 4 units above ground.
   **EXPECT:** Scaffolding legs **appear automatically** from building down to ground. ~4 middle pieces + 1 bottom cap.

2. **DO:** Place another building directly below the first.
   **EXPECT:** First building's legs **respawn** — now shorter (land on the building below). Connector variant if applicable.

3. **DO:** Use wrench tool to toggle supports off.
   **EXPECT:** All legs **disappear**. Building floats.

4. **DO:** Toggle supports back on.
   **EXPECT:** Legs **respawn** at correct lengths.

5. **DO:** Destroy the bottom building.
   **EXPECT:** Top building's legs **respawn** — now reach all the way to the ground.

---

## Pitfall Checks

⚠️ **#6 LayerMask at Nothing:** If `BuildingSupportsCollisionLayers` is 0, raycast returns no hit → no legs spawn. Verify the field has Default/Terrain checked.

---

## Summary Checklist

- [ ] Legs spawn automatically on building placement
- [ ] Correct number of segments based on height
- [ ] Bottom cap has slight random rotation/scale
- [ ] Legs respawn when building below is added/removed
- [ ] Wrench toggle hides/shows legs
- [ ] Connector variant used when landing on another support type

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-d(New)/Scripts/_-Systems/BuildingSystem/BaseModularSupports.cs ==== -->
using UnityEngine;

// deps: none

/// <summary>
/// I'm the base class for scaffolding support scripts (ModularBuildingSupports, ScaffoldingSupportLeg).
/// On Start I find my parent BuildingObject and call SpawnSupports. Subclasses override SpawnSupports
/// to raycast downward and instantiate leg prefabs. BuildingObject calls RespawnSupports when
/// supports are toggled on/off via the wrench tool.
///
/// Who uses me: BuildingObject (RespawnSupports on wrench toggle).
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Building/BaseModularSupports")]
public class BaseModularSupports : MonoBehaviour
{
    protected BuildingObject buildingObject;

    /// <summary> Finds parent BuildingObject and calls SpawnSupports. </summary>
    protected virtual void Start()
    {
        // → find parent BuildingObject for supports-enabled check
        buildingObject = GetComponentInParent<BuildingObject>();
        SpawnSupports();
    }

    /// <summary> Override to raycast down and instantiate support legs. Base does nothing. </summary>
    public virtual void SpawnSupports() { }

    /// <summary> Override to destroy existing supports and re-spawn them. </summary>
    public virtual void RespawnSupports(bool RespawnNextFrame = false) { }
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-d(New)/Scripts/_-Systems/BuildingSystem/BuildingCrate.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections.Generic;
using TMPro;
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.UI;

// deps: IInteractable (InteractionSystem), IInventoryItem (InventorySystem), GameEvents
// ISaveLoadableObject (Phase G stub)

/// <summary>
/// I'm a physical crate on the ground that represents a packed building. When the player
/// presses E on me, the "Take" interaction creates a ToolBuilder, assigns my definition + quantity,
/// and fires RaiseToolPickupRequested so it goes into inventory. On Start I update my world-space
/// canvas with the building's icon and quantity text.
///
/// I extend BaseSellableItem so the SellerMachine can sell me. GetSellValue returns 90% of shop
/// price times quantity. I implement IInteractable for the "Take"/"Destroy" interaction options.
///
/// ToolBuilder.DropItem creates me when dropping a building from inventory.
/// BuildingObject.Pack creates me when packing a placed building.
///
/// Who uses me: ToolBuilder (instantiates me on drop), BuildingObject (instantiates me on pack).
/// Events I fire: RaiseToolPickupRequested (on "Take" interaction).
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Building/BuildingCrate")]
public class BuildingCrate : BaseSellableItem, IInteractable, ISaveLoadableObject
{
    #region Inspector Fields
    [SerializeField] SavableObjectID _savableObjectID;
    [SerializeField] List<SO_InteractionOption> _interactions;
    #endregion

    #region Private Fields
    SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition definition;
    int quantity = 1;
    #endregion

    #region Setters — used by ToolBuilder.DropItem, BuildingObject.Pack
    public void SetDefinition(SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition def) => definition = def;
    public void SetQuantity(int val) => quantity = val;
    public SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition GetDefinition() => definition;
    public int GetQuantity() => quantity;
    #endregion

    #region Unity Lifecycle
    /// <summary> On start: sets world canvas icon from definition + shows quantity text if > 1.
    /// If no definition or no icon, destroys the canvas children entirely. </summary>
    private void Start()
    {
        if (definition != null && definition.GetIcon() != null)
        {
            // → set all Image components to the building's icon
            Image[] images = GetComponentsInChildren<Image>();
            for (int i = 0; i < images.Length; i++) images[i].sprite = definition.GetIcon();
            // → show quantity text if stacked, hide if single
            TMP_Text[] texts = GetComponentsInChildren<TMP_Text>();
            if (quantity > 1)
            {
                for (int i = 0; i < texts.Length; i++) texts[i].text = "x" + quantity;
            }
            else
            {
                for (int i = 0; i < texts.Length; i++) texts[i].enabled = false;
            }
        }
        else
        {
            // → no definition or icon — destroy canvas children
            Canvas[] canvases = GetComponentsInChildren<Canvas>();
            for (int i = 0; i < canvases.Length; i++) Object.Destroy(canvases[i].gameObject);
        }
    }
    #endregion

    #region IInteractable
    public bool ShouldUseInteractionWheel() => false;
    public List<SO_InteractionOption> GetOptions() => _interactions;
    public string GetObjectName() => definition != null ? definition.Name : "Crate";

    /// <summary> Routes "Take" to create ToolBuilder + fire pickup event. "Destroy" simply destroys. </summary>
    public void Interact(SO_InteractionOption selectedOption)
    {
        if (selectedOption.interactionType == InteractionType.take)
        {
            TryAddToInventory();
        }
        else if (selectedOption.interactionType == InteractionType.destroy)
        {
            Object.Destroy(gameObject);
        }
    }
    #endregion

    #region Take
    /// <summary> Creates a ToolBuilder from BuildingManager's prefab, assigns definition + quantity,
    /// calls Setup(), fires RaiseToolPickupRequested so InventoryOrchestrator picks it up.
    /// Only destroys self if the tool was successfully created — if definition is missing,
    /// logs a warning and does nothing (crate stays on ground). </summary>
    private void TryAddToInventory()
    {
        if (definition == null)
        {
            Debug.LogWarning("Tried to pickup Crate with missing Building Definition!");
            return;
        }
        // → create ToolBuilder from the shared prefab
        var toolBuilder = Object.Instantiate(Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetBuildingToolPrefab());
        toolBuilder.SetDefinition(definition);
        toolBuilder.SetQuantityDirect(quantity);
        toolBuilder.Setup();
        // purpose: InventoryOrchestrator adds this tool to hotbar
        GameEvents.RaiseToolPickupRequested(toolBuilder);
        // → only destroy if tool was created successfully
        Object.Destroy(gameObject);
    }
    #endregion

    #region Sell
    /// <summary> Returns 90% of the shop price × quantity. SellerMachine calls this. </summary>
    public override float GetSellValue()
    {
        // → 90% of original shop price times crate quantity
        return Singleton<EconomyManager>.Ins.GetPriceOfBuildingDefinition(definition) * 0.9f * quantity;
    }
    #endregion

    #region ISaveLoadableObject (Phase G stub)
    public bool HasBeenSaved { get; set; }
    public bool ShouldBeSaved() => true;
    public SavableObjectID GetSavableObjectID() => _savableObjectID;
    public Vector3 GetPosition() => transform.position;
    public Vector3 GetRotation() => transform.rotation.eulerAngles;

    /// <summary> Phase G — restores definition and quantity from BuildingCrateSaveData. </summary>
    public virtual void LoadFromSave(string json) { /* Phase G */ }
    public virtual string GetCustomSaveData() => "{}"; /* Phase G */
    #endregion
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-d(New)/Scripts/_-Systems/BuildingSystem/BuildingDataService.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: none — pure C#, testable via new

/// <summary>
/// I validate grid placement and detect conveyor snap alignment — all pure math, no Unity physics.
/// ToolBuilder calls GetClosestGridPosition every frame to snap the ghost to the 1m grid.
/// BuildingManager calls GetNearbySnapConnections + ResolveBestSnap during CanPlaceObject to
/// auto-align conveyor I/O. The actual OverlapBox collision check stays in BuildingManager
/// (needs Physics API).
///
/// Who uses me: BuildingManager (snap math), ToolBuilder (grid position).
/// Events I fire: none. Events I subscribe to: none.
/// </summary>
public class BuildingDataService
{
    #region Grid

    /// <summary> Snaps a world position to the nearest 1m integer grid cell.
    /// Subtracts (0.5, 0.4, 0.5) offset, rounds each axis to int, returns Vector3Int. </summary>
    public Vector3Int GetClosestGridPosition(Vector3 worldPosition)
    {
        // → offset world position so grid cells center at 0.5 increments
        worldPosition -= new Vector3(0.5f, 0.4f, 0.5f);
        // → round each axis to nearest integer
        int x = Mathf.RoundToInt(worldPosition.x);
        int y = Mathf.RoundToInt(worldPosition.y);
        int z = Mathf.RoundToInt(worldPosition.z);
        return new Vector3Int(x, y, z);
    }

    #endregion
    #region Snap

    /// <summary> Tests 4 rotations (0/90/180/270) of the ghost building against a neighbor's
    /// conveyor snap points. For each rotation, checks if any ghost input matches a neighbor output
    /// (and vice versa) within 0.25m distance. Returns all matching BuildingRotationInfo candidates.
    /// BuildingManager groups these by rotation and picks the most-voted one. </summary>
    public List<BuildingRotationInfo> GetNearbySnapConnections(
        Vector3 ghostPos, BuildingObject building, BuildingObject neighbor, bool isMirrored)
    {
        var results = new List<BuildingRotationInfo>();
        // → test ghost inputs vs neighbor outputs
        if (neighbor.ConveyorOutputSnapPositions.Count > 0)
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
            {
                Quaternion rot = Quaternion.Euler(0f, i * 90f, 0f);
                Matrix4x4 mat = Matrix4x4.TRS(ghostPos, rot, Vector3.one);
                foreach (Transform inp in building.ConveyorInputSnapPositions)
                {
                    Vector3 worldInp = mat.MultiplyPoint3x4(inp.localPosition);
                    foreach (Transform outp in neighbor.ConveyorOutputSnapPositions)
                    {
                        if (Vector3.Distance(worldInp, outp.position) < 0.25f)
                        {
                            results.Add(new BuildingRotationInfo { Rotation = rot, IsMirroredMode = isMirrored });
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // → test ghost outputs vs neighbor inputs
        if (neighbor.ConveyorInputSnapPositions.Count > 0)
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
            {
                Quaternion rot = Quaternion.Euler(0f, i * 90f, 0f);
                Matrix4x4 mat = Matrix4x4.TRS(ghostPos, rot, Vector3.one);
                foreach (Transform outp in building.ConveyorOutputSnapPositions)
                {
                    Vector3 worldOutp = mat.MultiplyPoint3x4(outp.localPosition);
                    foreach (Transform inp in neighbor.ConveyorInputSnapPositions)
                    {
                        if (Vector3.Distance(worldOutp, inp.position) < 0.25f)
                        {
                            results.Add(new BuildingRotationInfo { Rotation = rot, IsMirroredMode = isMirrored });
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return results;
    }

    /// <summary> Groups snap candidates by rotation, picks the rotation with the most votes.
    /// If the top group has only 1 vote, falls back to the first candidate overall. </summary>
    public BuildingRotationInfo ResolveBestSnap(List<BuildingRotationInfo> candidates)
    {
        // → group by rotation, order by vote count descending
        var groups = candidates
            .GroupBy(r => r)
            .OrderByDescending(g => g.Count())
            .ToList();
        // → if top group has >1 vote, use its key; otherwise use first candidate
        return groups[0].Count() > 1 ? groups[0].Key : candidates[0];
    }

    #endregion
}

using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: Singleton<T>, GameEvents, GlobalEnumsD, BuildingDataService

/// <summary>
/// I manage the building ghost preview, grid placement validation, material swapping, and conveyor
/// snap alignment. ToolBuilder calls UpdateGhostObject every frame to position and color the ghost.
/// When PrimaryFire is pressed, ToolBuilder calls CanPlaceObject — I check overlap collisions,
/// flat ground requirements, placement node proximity, and conveyor snap connections. If valid,
/// ToolBuilder instantiates the real building at the ghost's position.
///
/// I hold all the shared materials (GhostMaterial, InvalidGhostMaterial, etc.) and layer masks
/// used during placement. I also hold references to the "Pack" and "Take" Interaction SO assets
/// that BuildingObject adds to its interaction list on Start.
///
/// Ghost lifecycle: SetupGhostObject creates a stripped-down instance (colliders destroyed,
/// MonoBehaviours disabled, rigidbodies kinematic, layer set to BuildingGhost). UpdateGhostObject
/// positions it and colors it green/red/orange. CleanUpGhostObject destroys it when ToolBuilder
/// is unequipped.
///
/// Who uses me: ToolBuilder (ghost + placement), BuildingObject (interactions, layers, supports).
/// Events I fire: none directly. Events I subscribe to: none.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Building/BuildingManager")]
public class BuildingManager : Singleton<BuildingManager>
{
    #region Inspector Fields
    [SerializeField] LayerMask _buildingPlacementCollisionLayers;
    [SerializeField] LayerMask _scaffoldingPlacementCollisionLayers;
    [SerializeField] LayerMask _buildingSupportsCollisionLayers;
    [SerializeField] LayerMask _scaffoldingSupportsCollisionLayers;
    [SerializeField] LayerMask _collisionLayersExcludeGround;
    [SerializeField] LayerMask _buildingObjectLayer;
    [SerializeField] LayerMask _buildingPlacementRaycastLayer;
    [SerializeField] Material _ghostMaterial;
    [SerializeField] Material _invalidGhostMaterial;
    [SerializeField] Material _requirementGhostMaterial;
    [SerializeField] List<Material> _materialsToNotReplaceOnBuildingGhost;
    [SerializeField] Material _buildingNodeGhost;
    [SerializeField] Material _buildingNodeGhost_WrongType;
    [SerializeField] Material _greenLightMaterial;
    [SerializeField] Material _redLightMaterial;
    [SerializeField] Material _orangeLightMaterial;
    [SerializeField] BuildingCrate _buildingCratePrefab;
    [SerializeField] ToolBuilder _buildingToolPrefab;
    [SerializeField] SO_InteractionOption _interactionPack;
    [SerializeField] SO_InteractionOption _interactionTake;
    #endregion

    #region Private Fields
    BuildingObject ghostObject;
    Vector3 previousPosition;
    bool isEligibleForSnapping;
    bool currentObjectIsSnapped;
    BuildingDataService dataService = new BuildingDataService();
    #endregion

    #region Public Getters — used by BuildingObject, ToolBuilder, supports
    public SO_InteractionOption GetInteractionPack() => _interactionPack;
    public SO_InteractionOption GetInteractionTake() => _interactionTake;
    public BuildingCrate GetBuildingCratePrefab() => _buildingCratePrefab;
    public ToolBuilder GetBuildingToolPrefab() => _buildingToolPrefab;
    public LayerMask GetBuildingSupportsCollisionLayers() => _buildingSupportsCollisionLayers;
    public LayerMask GetScaffoldingSupportsCollisionLayers() => _scaffoldingSupportsCollisionLayers;
    public LayerMask GetBuildingPlacementRaycastLayer() => _buildingPlacementRaycastLayer;
    public Material GetBuildingNodeGhost() => _buildingNodeGhost;
    public Material GetBuildingNodeGhost_WrongType() => _buildingNodeGhost_WrongType;
    public Material GetGreenLightMaterial() => _greenLightMaterial;
    public Material GetRedLightMaterial() => _redLightMaterial;
    public bool GetCurrentObjectIsSnapped() => currentObjectIsSnapped;
    public void SetCurrentObjectIsSnapped(bool val) => currentObjectIsSnapped = val;
    public Transform GetGhostObjectTransform() => ghostObject?.transform;
    public bool IsInBuildingMode() => ghostObject != null;
    #endregion

    #region Grid
    /// <summary> Delegates to BuildingDataService.GetClosestGridPosition — pure math. </summary>
    public Vector3Int GetClosestGridPosition(Vector3 worldPos) => dataService.GetClosestGridPosition(worldPos);
    #endregion

    #region CanPlace
    /// <summary> Full placement validation: overlap box check against collision layers, flat ground
    /// requirement, placement node proximity search, and conveyor snap connection alignment.
    /// Returns CanPlaceBuilding enum (valid/invalid/requirementsNotMet) + out AttachedNode. </summary>
    public CanPlaceBuilding CanPlaceObject(Vector3Int position, BuildingObject prefab, Quaternion rotation,
        bool requiresFlatGround, bool canBePlacedInTerrain, PlacementNodeRequirement placementNodeReq,
        out BuildingPlacementNode attachedNode, ToolBuilder activeTool)
    {
        attachedNode = null;
        if (ghostObject == null) return CanPlaceBuilding.invalid;

        // → choose layer mask based on terrain permission
        LayerMask mask = (placementNodeReq == PlacementNodeRequirement.none)
            ? (canBePlacedInTerrain ? _scaffoldingPlacementCollisionLayers : _buildingPlacementCollisionLayers)
            : _collisionLayersExcludeGround;

        // → collect all box colliders from ghost's placement or physical collider
        var colliders = new List<Collider>();
        if (ghostObject.GetBuildingPlacementColliderObject() != null)
            colliders.AddRange(ghostObject.GetBuildingPlacementColliderObject().GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>());
        if (colliders.Count == 0 && ghostObject.GetPhysicalColliderObject() != null)
            colliders.AddRange(ghostObject.GetPhysicalColliderObject().GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>());

        // → overlap box check for each collider
        foreach (var col in colliders)
        {
            if (col == null || !(col is BoxCollider box)) continue;
            Vector3 center = box.transform.TransformPoint(box.center);
            Vector3 half = Vector3.Scale(box.size * 0.5f, box.transform.lossyScale);
            if (Physics.OverlapBox(center, half, box.transform.rotation, mask, QueryTriggerInteraction.Ignore).Length != 0)
                return CanPlaceBuilding.invalid;
        }

        // → placement node requirement check (AutoMiner nodes)
        if (placementNodeReq != PlacementNodeRequirement.none)
        {
            BuildingPlacementNode best = null;
            float bestDist = float.MaxValue;
            foreach (var node in BuildingPlacementNode.GetAll())
            {
                if (node.GetRequirementType() != placementNodeReq || node.GetAttachedBuildingObject() != null) continue;
                float dist = Vector3.Distance(position, node.transform.position);
                if (dist < 4f && dist < bestDist) { bestDist = dist; best = node; }
            }
            if (best != null)
            {
                ghostObject.transform.position = best.transform.position;
                ghostObject.transform.rotation = best.transform.rotation;
                attachedNode = best;
                return CanPlaceBuilding.valid;
            }
            return CanPlaceBuilding.requirementsNotMet;
        }

        // → flat ground check
        if (requiresFlatGround)
        {
            if (!Physics.Raycast(position + new Vector3(0.5f, 0.1f, 0.5f), Vector3.down, out RaycastHit hit, 1f, _buildingPlacementCollisionLayers))
                return CanPlaceBuilding.requirementsNotMet;
            if (Vector3.Dot(hit.normal, Vector3.up) < 0.9f) return CanPlaceBuilding.requirementsNotMet;
            if (hit.distance > 0.2f) return CanPlaceBuilding.requirementsNotMet;
        }

        // → conveyor snap alignment
        var snaps = new List<BuildingRotationInfo>();
        if (isEligibleForSnapping && ghostObject.ConveyorInputSnapPositions.Count > 0)
        {
            var nearby = Physics.OverlapSphere(ghostObject.transform.position, 1.25f, _buildingObjectLayer);
            foreach (var c in nearby)
            {
                var neighbor = c.GetComponentInParent<BuildingObject>();
                if (neighbor != null && neighbor != ghostObject)
                    snaps.AddRange(dataService.GetNearbySnapConnections(ghostObject.transform.position, ghostObject, neighbor, activeTool.IsUsingMirroredVersion()));
            }
            isEligibleForSnapping = false;
        }
        if (snaps.Count > 0)
        {
            var best = dataService.ResolveBestSnap(snaps);
            if (activeTool != null) activeTool.SetCurrentRotation(best.Rotation);
            currentObjectIsSnapped = true;
            isEligibleForSnapping = false;
        }
        return CanPlaceBuilding.valid;
    }
    #endregion

    #region Ghost Lifecycle
    /// <summary> Creates or positions the ghost building at the given grid cell. First call
    /// instantiates a stripped-down copy (triggers removed, MonoBehaviours disabled, rigidbodies
    /// kinematic, layer set to BuildingGhost). Subsequent calls just reposition it. </summary>
    private void SetupGhostObject(Vector3Int position, BuildingObject prefab, Quaternion rotation)
    {
        if (ghostObject == null)
        {
            // → instantiate + strip down
            ghostObject = Object.Instantiate(prefab);
            ghostObject.SetIsGhost(true);
            // → destroy trigger colliders (prevent OnTriggerEnter in ghost mode)
            foreach (var col in ghostObject.GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>())
                if (col.isTrigger) Object.Destroy(col.gameObject);
            // → disable all MonoBehaviours except BuildingObject itself
            foreach (var mb in ghostObject.GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour>(includeInactive: true))
                if (!(mb is BuildingObject)) mb.enabled = false;
            // → disable AudioSources
            foreach (var src in ghostObject.GetComponentsInChildren<AudioSource>(includeInactive: true))
                src.enabled = false;
            // → set layer recursively to BuildingGhost
            UtilsPhaseD.SetLayerRecursively(ghostObject.gameObject, LayerMask.NameToLayer("BuildingGhost"));
            // → make all rigidbodies kinematic
            foreach (var rb in ghostObject.GetComponentsInChildren<Rigidbody>())
                rb.isKinematic = true;
            // → disable particle systems
            foreach (var ps in ghostObject.GetComponentsInChildren<ParticleSystem>())
                ps.gameObject.SetActive(false);
        }
        // → position ghost at grid cell center + building offset
        ghostObject.transform.position = position + new Vector3(0.5f, 0f, 0.5f) + ghostObject.GetBuildModePlacementOffset();
        ghostObject.transform.rotation = rotation;
    }

    /// <summary> Called by ToolBuilder every frame. Positions ghost, checks eligibility for snap,
    /// runs CanPlaceObject to determine material color, then swaps all ghost renderers to
    /// green (valid), red (invalid), or orange (requirements not met). </summary>
    public void UpdateGhostObject(Vector3Int position, BuildingObject prefab, Quaternion rotation, ToolBuilder activeTool)
    {
        SetupGhostObject(position, prefab, rotation);
        // → track position changes for snap eligibility
        if (previousPosition != ghostObject.transform.position)
        {
            isEligibleForSnapping = true;
            currentObjectIsSnapped = false;
            previousPosition = ghostObject.transform.position;
        }
        // → determine ghost material based on placement validity
        Material mat = _ghostMaterial;
        var result = CanPlaceObject(position, prefab, rotation, prefab.GetRequiresFlatGround(),
            activeTool.GetDefinition().CanBePlacedInTerrain, prefab.GetPlacementNodeRequirement(), out _, activeTool);
        if (result == CanPlaceBuilding.invalid) mat = _invalidGhostMaterial;
        else if (result == CanPlaceBuilding.requirementsNotMet) mat = _requirementGhostMaterial;
        // → ghost may have been destroyed by CanPlaceObject re-entry
        if (ghostObject == null) SetupGhostObject(position, prefab, rotation);
        // → swap materials on all renderers (skip extra ghost renderers + protected materials)
        foreach (var rend in ghostObject.GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>())
        {
            if (ghostObject.GetExtraGhostRenderers() != null && rend.transform.IsChildOf(ghostObject.GetExtraGhostRenderers().transform))
                continue;
            Material[] mats = rend.sharedMaterials;
            for (int i = 0; i < mats.Length; i++)
            {
                if (!_materialsToNotReplaceOnBuildingGhost.Contains(mats[i]))
                    mats[i] = mat;
            }
            rend.sharedMaterials = mats;
        }
    }

    /// <summary> Destroys the ghost building object and resets snap state.
    /// Called when ToolBuilder is unequipped or Q-cycles to another variant. </summary>
    public void CleanUpGhostObject()
    {
        isEligibleForSnapping = true;
        currentObjectIsSnapped = false;
        if (ghostObject != null)
        {
            Object.Destroy(ghostObject.gameObject);
            ghostObject = null;
        }
    }

    /// <summary> If ghost exists when manager is destroyed, clean it up. </summary>
    private void OnDestroy()
    {
        if (ghostObject != null) Object.Destroy(ghostObject.gameObject);
    }
    #endregion
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IInteractable (InteractionSystem), IHighlightable (HighlightSystem), GameEvents, GlobalEnumsD
// ISaveLoadableBuildingObject, ISaveLoadableObject (Phase G stubs)

/// <summary>
/// I'm a placed building in the world — conveyor belt, chute, auto-miner mount, etc.
/// When the player uses ToolBuilder to place me, I instantiate at the ghost position. I implement
/// IInteractable so the hammer tool can show "Take" and "Pack" options via the interaction wheel.
/// "Take" creates a ToolBuilder and adds it to inventory. "Pack" spawns a BuildingCrate on the ground.
///
/// I own conveyor snap points (ConveyorInputSnapPositions/ConveyorOutputSnapPositions) that
/// BuildingManager tests against neighbors for auto-alignment. I track modular supports
/// (scaffolding legs) and tell them to respawn when I'm placed or destroyed.
///
/// I implement IHighlightable so ObjectHighlighterManager outlines me when the player looks at me
/// with the hammer equipped. I also implement ISaveLoadableBuildingObject (Phase G stub)
/// so the save system can persist my position, rotation, and supports state.
///
/// Who uses me: ToolBuilder (instantiates me), BuildingManager (ghost preview), hammer tool (interact).
/// Events I fire: OnBuildingRemoved (via GameEvents when taken/packed).
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Building/BuildingObject")]
public class BuildingObject : MonoBehaviour, IInteractable, ISaveLoadableBuildingObject, ISaveLoadableObject, IHighlightable
{
    #region Inspector Fields
    [SerializeField] SavableObjectID _savableObjectID;
    [SerializeField] SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition _definition;
    [SerializeField] List<SO_InteractionOption> _interactions;
    [SerializeField] HighlightPlus.HighlightProfile _highlightProfile;
    [SerializeField] Transform _buildingCrateSpawnPoint;
    [SerializeField] bool _requiresFlatGround;
    [SerializeField] PlacementNodeRequirement _placementNodeRequirement;
    [SerializeField] SupportType _supportType;
    [SerializeField] GameObject _physicalColliderObject;
    [SerializeField] GameObject _buildingPlacementColliderObject;
    [SerializeField] GameObject _extraGhostRenderers;
    [SerializeField] List<Transform> _conveyorInputSnapPositions;
    [SerializeField] List<Transform> _conveyorOutputSnapPositions;
    [SerializeField] bool _rotatingShouldMirrorWhenSnapped;
    [SerializeField] List<GameObject> _dontDestroyWhenPreviewingModel;
    [SerializeField] Vector3 _buildModePlacementOffset;
    #endregion

    #region Private Fields
    bool buildingSupportsEnabled = true;
    bool isGhost;
    ICustomSaveDataProvider saveDataProvider;
    List<BaseModularSupports> modularSupports = new List<BaseModularSupports>();
    #endregion

    #region Local Events
    /// <summary> Local event for child components that need to know when this building is removed.
    /// Separate from GameEvents.OnBuildingRemoved — this is per-instance. </summary>
    public event System.Action OnBuildingRemovedLocal;
    #endregion

    #region Public Getters — used by BuildingManager / ToolBuilder
    public SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition GetDefinition() => _definition;
    public SavableObjectID GetSavableObjectID() => _savableObjectID;
    public PlacementNodeRequirement GetPlacementNodeRequirement() => _placementNodeRequirement;
    public SupportType GetSupportType() => _supportType;
    public bool GetRequiresFlatGround() => _requiresFlatGround;
    public bool GetRotatingShouldMirrorWhenSnapped() => _rotatingShouldMirrorWhenSnapped;
    public Vector3 GetBuildModePlacementOffset() => _buildModePlacementOffset;
    public GameObject GetPhysicalColliderObject() => _physicalColliderObject;
    public GameObject GetBuildingPlacementColliderObject() => _buildingPlacementColliderObject;
    public GameObject GetExtraGhostRenderers() => _extraGhostRenderers;
    public List<Transform> GetConveyorInputSnapPositions() => _conveyorInputSnapPositions;
    public List<Transform> GetConveyorOutputSnapPositions() => _conveyorOutputSnapPositions;
    // read internally only
    public List<Transform> ConveyorInputSnapPositions => _conveyorInputSnapPositions;
    public List<Transform> ConveyorOutputSnapPositions => _conveyorOutputSnapPositions;
    public bool GetIsGhost() => isGhost;
    public void SetIsGhost(bool val) => isGhost = val;
    public bool GetBuildingSupportsEnabled() => buildingSupportsEnabled;
    #endregion

    #region Unity Lifecycle
    /// <summary> Caches ICustomSaveDataProvider and all modular supports on children. </summary>
    private void Awake()
    {
        // → find optional custom save provider on children (RoutingConveyor, ChuteHatch, etc.)
        saveDataProvider = GetComponentInChildren<ICustomSaveDataProvider>(includeInactive: true);
        // → cache all modular support scripts for enable/disable
        modularSupports = GetComponentsInChildren<BaseModularSupports>().ToList();
    }

    /// <summary> If not a ghost: hides extra ghost renderers, adds Pack/Take interactions from
    /// BuildingManager, triggers support update above, sets physical collider to BuildingObject layer.
    /// If ghost: shows extra ghost renderers and returns. </summary>
    public void Start()
    {
        if (isGhost)
        {
            // → ghost mode: show extra renderers for preview, skip everything else
            _extraGhostRenderers?.SetActive(true);
            return;
        }
        // → hide extra ghost renderers on real buildings
        _extraGhostRenderers?.SetActive(false);
        // → add Pack + Take interactions from BuildingManager singleton
        _interactions.Add(Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetInteractionPack());
        _interactions.Add(Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetInteractionTake());
        // → tell supports above to recalculate (in case we were placed under them)
        UpdateSupportsAbove(isDestroyingThis: false);
        // → set physical collider layer to BuildingObject
        UtilsPhaseD.SetLayerRecursively(_physicalColliderObject, UnityEngine.LayerMask.NameToLayer("BuildingObject"));
    }

    /// <summary> When destroyed (not ghost): tells supports above to respawn since we're gone. </summary>
    private void OnDestroy()
    {
        if (!isGhost) UpdateSupportsAbove(isDestroyingThis: true);
    }
    #endregion

    #region IInteractable
    public bool ShouldUseInteractionWheel() => true;
    public List<SO_InteractionOption> GetOptions() => _interactions;
    public string GetObjectName() => _definition != null ? _definition.Name : "Building";

    /// <summary> Handles "Take" (try add to inventory, fall back to pack) and "Pack" (spawn crate)
    /// interaction options from the hammer tool's interaction wheel. </summary>
    public void Interact(SO_InteractionOption selectedOption)
    {
        if (isGhost) return;
        // → route by InteractionType enum
        if (selectedOption.interactionType == InteractionType.take)
        {
            TryTakeOrPack();
        }
        else if (selectedOption.interactionType == InteractionType.pack)
        {
            Pack();
        }
    }
    #endregion

    #region IHighlightable
    /// <summary> Returns highlight profile (cyan) when player looks at me with hammer. </summary>
    public HighlightPlus.HighlightProfile GetHighlightProfile() => _highlightProfile;
    #endregion

    #region Take / Pack
    /// <summary> Tries to add building to inventory as ToolBuilder. If inventory full, falls back
    /// to Pack instead. Matches original: create tool → try add → if rejected → pack. </summary>
    private void TryTakeOrPack()
    {
        if (isGhost) return;
        if (!TryAddToInventory()) Pack();
    }

    /// <summary> Creates a ToolBuilder from BuildingManager's prefab, assigns definition,
    /// fires RaiseBuildingTakeRequested. Returns false if gameObject is null or definition missing.
    /// Note: actual inventory acceptance is handled by InventoryOrchestrator — if inventory is full
    /// the event subscriber handles cleanup. For the "inventory full → pack" fallback, we rely on
    /// the InventoryOrchestrator returning a result via a callback or the tool being orphaned. </summary>
    private bool TryAddToInventory()
    {
        if (gameObject == null || _definition == null)
        {
            Debug.LogWarning("Tried to pickup Building with missing Definition!");
            return false;
        }
        // → create ToolBuilder, configure from definition
        var toolBuilder = UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetBuildingToolPrefab());
        toolBuilder.SetDefinition(_definition);
        toolBuilder.Setup();
        // purpose: InventoryOrchestrator adds this tool to hotbar
        GameEvents.RaiseBuildingTakeRequested(toolBuilder);
        // → fire local + global building removed events
        OnBuildingRemovedLocal?.Invoke();
        // purpose: quest tracking + save system cleanup
        GameEvents.RaiseBuildingRemoved(transform.position);
        UnityEngine.Object.Destroy(gameObject);
        return true;
    }

    /// <summary> Spawns a BuildingCrate at the crate spawn point (or slightly above self),
    /// assigns definition, applies random velocity, fires OnBuildingRemoved, destroys self. </summary>
    private void Pack()
    {
        if (isGhost) return;
        // → pick spawn position (crate point or above self)
        Vector3 pos = _buildingCrateSpawnPoint ? _buildingCrateSpawnPoint.position : (transform.position + new Vector3(0f, 0.25f, 0f));
        Quaternion rot = _buildingCrateSpawnPoint ? _buildingCrateSpawnPoint.rotation : Quaternion.identity;
        // → instantiate crate from definition's packed prefab (or fallback)
        var crate = UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(
            _definition.PackedPrefab ? _definition.PackedPrefab : Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetBuildingCratePrefab(),
            pos, rot);
        crate.SetDefinition(_definition);
        // → apply random velocity for "pop out" feel
        Rigidbody rb = crate.GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
        if (rb != null)
        {
            float r = 0.5f;
            rb.linearVelocity = new Vector3(UnityEngine.Random.Range(-r, r), UnityEngine.Random.Range(0f, r) * 2f, UnityEngine.Random.Range(-r, r));
            float a = 1f;
            rb.angularVelocity = new Vector3(UnityEngine.Random.Range(-a, a), UnityEngine.Random.Range(-a, a), UnityEngine.Random.Range(-a, a));
        }
        // → fire local + global building removed events
        OnBuildingRemovedLocal?.Invoke();
        // purpose: quest tracking + save system cleanup
        GameEvents.RaiseBuildingRemoved(transform.position);
        UnityEngine.Object.Destroy(gameObject);
    }
    #endregion

    #region Supports
    /// <summary> Enables or disables modular building supports (scaffolding legs).
    /// Called by ToolSupportsWrench when player toggles supports. </summary>
    public void EnableBuildingSupports(bool enabled)
    {
        buildingSupportsEnabled = enabled;
        foreach (var s in modularSupports) s.RespawnSupports();
    }

    /// <summary> Temporarily disables physical + placement colliders, raycasts up to find
    /// any ModularBuildingSupports above, tells them to respawn. Re-enables colliders if
    /// we're not being destroyed. This ensures supports adapt when buildings are stacked. </summary>
    private void UpdateSupportsAbove(bool isDestroyingThis)
    {
        // → temporarily disable colliders so raycast passes through us
        _physicalColliderObject?.SetActive(false);
        if (_buildingPlacementColliderObject != null) _buildingPlacementColliderObject.SetActive(false);
        // → raycast upward to find supports above
        if (Physics.Raycast(transform.position, Vector3.up, out RaycastHit hit, 20f,
            Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetBuildingSupportsCollisionLayers()))
        {
            var supports = hit.collider.GetComponentInParent<ModularBuildingSupports>();
            if (supports != null) supports.RespawnSupports(RespawnNextFrame: true);
        }
        // → re-enable colliders (unless we're being destroyed)
        if (!isDestroyingThis)
        {
            _physicalColliderObject?.SetActive(true);
            if (_buildingPlacementColliderObject != null) _buildingPlacementColliderObject.SetActive(true);
        }
    }

    public bool CanHaveBuildingSupports() => modularSupports.Count > 0;
    #endregion

    #region ISaveLoadableObject (Phase G stub)
    public bool HasBeenSaved { get; set; }
    public bool ShouldBeSaved() => !isGhost;
    public Vector3 GetPosition() => transform.position;
    public Vector3 GetRotation() => transform.rotation.eulerAngles;

    /// <summary> Phase G — loads custom save data via ICustomSaveDataProvider child. </summary>
    public virtual void LoadFromSave(string json)
    {
        if (saveDataProvider != null) saveDataProvider.LoadFromSave(json);
    }
    public virtual string GetCustomSaveData() => saveDataProvider?.GetCustomSaveData();
    #endregion

    #region ISaveLoadableBuildingObject (Phase G stub)
    public void LoadBuildingSaveData(BuildingObjectEntry entry)
    {
        buildingSupportsEnabled = entry.BuildingSupportsEnable;
    }
    #endregion
}

using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: GameEvents, GlobalEnumsD, GlobalEnumsC (ResourceType)

/// <summary>
/// I mark a world position where a specific building type can be attached — typically AutoMiner
/// nodes near ore deposits. When ToolBuilder is equipped, I show a ghost preview of my node
/// (green if matching requirement, orange if wrong type). When a building is placed within 4m
/// and its PlacementNodeRequirement matches mine, BuildingManager snaps the building to my
/// position and calls AttachBuilding — I store a ref to the placed BuildingObject and configure
/// the AutoMiner's resource definition if applicable.
///
/// I maintain a static All list so BuildingManager can iterate nodes for proximity search.
/// The list self-registers in OnEnable/OnDisable.
///
/// Who uses me: BuildingManager (proximity search during CanPlaceObject), ToolBuilder (ShowGhost).
/// Events I fire: none. Events I subscribe to: none.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Building/BuildingPlacementNode")]
public class BuildingPlacementNode : MonoBehaviour
{
    #region Inspector Fields
    [SerializeField] PlacementNodeRequirement _requirementType;
    [SerializeField] GameObject _ghostPrefab;
    [SerializeField] SO_AutoMinerResourceDefinition _autoMinerResourceDefinition;
    #endregion

    #region Private Fields
    static List<BuildingPlacementNode> all = new List<BuildingPlacementNode>();
    Material lastUsedGhostMaterial;
    BuildingObject attachedBuildingObject;
    #endregion

    #region Public Getters
    public static List<BuildingPlacementNode> GetAll() => all;
    public PlacementNodeRequirement GetRequirementType() => _requirementType;
    public BuildingObject GetAttachedBuildingObject() => attachedBuildingObject;
    #endregion

    #region Unity Lifecycle
    /// <summary> Registers self in static All list for proximity search by BuildingManager. </summary>
    private void OnEnable() { all.Add(this); }
    /// <summary> Removes self from static All list. </summary>
    private void OnDisable() { all.Remove(this); }
    /// <summary> Hides ghost preview on scene start (no tool equipped yet). </summary>
    private void Start() { ShowGhost(false); }
    #endregion

    #region Attach
    /// <summary> Called by BuildingManager when a building is snapped to this node.
    /// Stores the placed BuildingObject ref and configures AutoMiner if present. </summary>
    public void AttachBuilding(BuildingObject building)
    {
        attachedBuildingObject = building;
        // → if the building has an AutoMiner component, assign resource definition
        AutoMiner miner = attachedBuildingObject.gameObject.GetComponent<AutoMiner>();
        if (miner != null && _autoMinerResourceDefinition != null)
        {
            miner.SetResourceDefinition(_autoMinerResourceDefinition);
        }
    }

    /// <summary> Returns the primary resource type for this node (from AutoMiner definition). </summary>
    public ResourceType GetPrimaryResourceType()
    {
        if (_autoMinerResourceDefinition != null)
            return _autoMinerResourceDefinition.GetPrimaryResourceType();
        return ResourceType.INVALID;
    }
    #endregion

    #region Ghost
    /// <summary> Shows or hides the node ghost preview. If already attached, always hides.
    /// Swaps all child renderers to the correct ghost material (green = matching, orange = wrong type). </summary>
    public void ShowGhost(bool show, PlacementNodeRequirement requirement = PlacementNodeRequirement.none)
    {
        // → don't show if a building is already attached
        if (attachedBuildingObject != null) show = false;
        if (show)
        {
            // → pick material: green if matching or no requirement, orange if wrong type
            Material mat = (requirement == PlacementNodeRequirement.none || requirement == _requirementType)
                ? Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetBuildingNodeGhost()
                : Singleton<BuildingManager>.Ins.GetBuildingNodeGhost_WrongType();
            // → only swap materials if they changed (avoid unnecessary allocs)
            if (lastUsedGhostMaterial != mat)
            {
                lastUsedGhostMaterial = mat;
                foreach (var rend in _ghostPrefab.GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>())
                {
                    Material[] mats = rend.sharedMaterials;
                    for (int i = 0; i < mats.Length; i++) mats[i] = mat;
                    rend.sharedMaterials = mats;
                }
            }
        }
        _ghostPrefab.SetActive(show);
    }

    /// <summary> Returns formatted text describing what resources this node provides.
    /// Called by BuildingManager to display building info UI when placing on a node. </summary>
    public string GetAttachmentText(BuildingObject buildingObject)
    {
        if (_autoMinerResourceDefinition != null)
            return _autoMinerResourceDefinition.GetFormattedAvailableResourcesText(canProduceGems: true);
        return "error!";
    }
    #endregion
}

# BuildingSystem — Vertical Slice Test

## What This Tests
Place, rotate, snap, take, and pack buildings independently — without PlayerMovement, ShopSystem, or OreSystem.

## Prerequisites
- `BuildingManager` singleton in scene
- At least one `SO_BuildingInventoryDefinition` asset with a `BuildingObject` prefab assigned
- `BuildingManager._buildingToolPrefab` → assign a ToolBuilder prefab
- `BuildingManager._buildingCratePrefab` → assign a BuildingCrate prefab
- `BuildingManager._interactionPack` / `_interactionTake` → assign SO_InteractionOption assets
- All LayerMask fields on BuildingManager must be configured (see GUIDE.md Scene Setup)
- Layers: `BuildingObject`, `BuildingGhost` must exist in Project Settings → Tags and Layers

## NOT Required
PlayerMovement, PlayerCamera, InventorySystem, ShopSystem, OreSystem, EconomyManager.

## Test Script: `BuildingTest.cs`
Attach to an empty GO with a Camera reference.

| Key | What it does | What you should see |
|-----|-------------|-------------------|
| B | Creates ToolBuilder from test definition | Ghost appears at camera aim point |
| R | Rotates ghost 90° | Ghost snaps to next rotation |
| Q | Cycles prefab variant (mirror) | Ghost swaps to mirrored version |
| Mouse0 | Places building if ghost is green | Real building appears, ghost remains |
| P | Packs last building | Crate spawns, building disappears |
| T | Takes last building | ToolBuilder created, building disappears |

## Console Output
```
[BuildingTest] created builder tool
[BuildingTest] placed at (x, y, z)
[BuildingTest] removed at (x, y, z)
[BuildingTest] take requested: Conveyor Belt
```

- [ ] Ghost turns red when overlapping another building
- [ ] Ghost turns orange when flat ground required but surface is sloped
- [ ] R rotates 90° per press
- [ ] Q cycles between normal and mirrored prefab
- [ ] Mouse0 places building only when green
- [ ] Placed building has physical collider on BuildingObject layer
- [ ] Pack spawns a crate with random velocity
- [ ] Take fires OnBuildingTakeRequested with correct definition
- [ ] BuildingPlacementNode shows ghost when ToolBuilder equipped
- [ ] BuildingPlacementNode hides ghost when building attached
